title: Consolidate the shared Boolean CPU/CUDA probe contract
finding: The packed CPU arm loaded the entire CUDA experiment with runpy only to reuse ProbeCase, deterministic fixture construction, bounds, the VRAM estimate, reference-operation counting, support comparison, ratios and report persistence. Those responsibilities therefore lived inside one physical backend script while a second physical backend depended on executing that script as a pseudo-library. Tests repeated the same runpy coupling. This was a parallel ownership seam and made CPU/CUDA comparisons vulnerable to accidental fixture drift.
gardener_decision: Move only the exact backend-neutral Boolean probe contract into one small sibling module. Keep CUDA execution in cuda_boolean_probe.py and packed CPU execution in cpu_bitset_baseline.py. Delete duplicated helpers and runpy coupling rather than adding a probe framework, backend registry, scheduler, store or second Tensor authority.
changes: add experiments/tensor_gpu/boolean_probe_contract.py as the sole owner of ProbeCase, shared bounds, deterministic fixture identity, explicit CUDA memory estimate, exact reference-operation count, support equality, diagnostic ratio and atomic report persistence
make both CUDA and packed-CPU arms import that exact shared contract while retaining direct-script execution
remove the duplicated ProbeCase/fixture/memory/comparison/report implementation from the CUDA arm
remove runpy and duplicated comparison helpers from the packed-CPU arm
make focused tests assert object identity for the shared contract and mechanically refuse runpy coupling
compile every experiment/tensor_gpu Python module through the existing Fourfold/Tensor workflow instead of maintaining another explicit file list

delta_from_pre_head.note: Net lines increase because one explicit shared contract and identity regressions replace hidden dynamic coupling; the CUDA physical arm itself loses 176 net lines and the same shared responsibilities are no longer owned twice.
